- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- Model consistently underestimates peaks in the 3rd–5th week of forecast horizon; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to peak predictions.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the following 2–3 days; apply a 1–3% downward correction.
- Model shows persistent mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days are below 65.00, forecast should not dip below 63.00 unless sentiment confirms strong bearish trend.
- Sentiment volatility > 0.5 in last 5 days correlates with model overfitting; reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% in such cases.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) for 3+ days, model tends to drift toward recent low; correct by adding 0.5–1.0% to avoid false bottoming.
